scenario: After a short imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a man convicted of reckless driving wants to organise a foundation for young victims of highway accidents. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 250,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. His victim, whose car was damaged, opposes such a foundation and considers it immoral. If I approve and accept the money for the foundation, victims of other accidents will benefit from the 250,000 dollars. If I do nothing, the money will be lost.
entities: 1 human: I, the president of the agency deciding about the foundation,1 human: the man convicted of reckless driving who wants to create the foundation and have it named after himself,1 human: the victim whose car was damaged and who opposes the foundation,an unspecified number of humans: other accident victims who would benefit from the $250,000 if the foundation were approved,I
outcomes: The 250,000 dollars is not given to the foundation
Victims of other highway accidents do not receive support from the 250,000 dollars
The convicted man does not get a foundation named after himself
The victim whose car was damaged is not faced with a foundation honoring the convicted man
